# Analyze the data for each country group separately
country_groups = df_education['Country Group'].unique()

# Initialize a dictionary to store the correlation results
correlation_results = {}

# Loop through each country group
for group in country_groups:
    # Filter the data for the current country group
    df_education_group = df_education[df_education['Country Group'] == group]
    df_gdp_group = df_gdp[df_gdp['Country Group'] == group]
    
    # Reshape the data into a long format
    df_education_long_group = df_education_group.melt(id_vars='Country Group', var_name='Year', value_name='Education_Expenditure')
    df_gdp_long_group = df_gdp_group.melt(id_vars='Country Group', var_name='Year', value_name='GDP')
    
    # Merge the education expenditure and GDP data
    df_analysis_group = pd.merge(df_education_long_group, df_gdp_long_group, on=['Country Group', 'Year'])
    
    # Calculate the correlation between education expenditure and GDP
    correlation = df_analysis_group[['Education_Expenditure', 'GDP']].corr().iloc[0, 1]
    correlation_results[group] = correlation

# Display the correlation results
correlation_results
